Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis  
Details: The failing test `testMissingRequiredOptions` is designed to verify that when a required option is missing from the parsed command line arguments, a `MissingOptionException` is thrown with a correctly formatted message listing the missing required options with their option names prefixed by '-'. The test expects the message: "Missing required options: b, c".  

The issue report states that the message format changed between CLI 1.0 and 1.1. In CLI 1.0, the messages included dashes before option names (e.g., "-format-source-properties"), while in CLI 1.1, the option names are shown without dashes, resulting in less readable messages. The report mentions that in CLI 1.0, `Options.addOption(Option)` was prefixing option keys with "-", but in CLI 1.1, it no longer prefixes options with "-".  

The inspected `Options.addOption(Option)` method shows it uses `opt.getKey()` to identify the option as its key, and simply stores it in collections without adding any prefix. The `Option.getKey()` method returns either the short option character (like 'c') or the long option string if present, directly without prefixing '-'. This confirms the change that in CLI 1.1, the option keys do not have the '-' prefix.  

Since `MissingOptionException` is constructed with these option keys and probably uses them to build the error message, the messages no longer contain the leading '-'. This is why the user sees messages like "formatsourceproperties" instead of "-format-source-properties".  

Hence, the root cause is that the keys stored for options and used in errors omit the '-' prefix, which was previously added inside `Options.addOption` or elsewhere in CLI 1.0, but is now missing in CLI 1.1. This breaks the formatting of the error messages by removing the '-' prefix expected by the user and tests.  

To fix this, the functionality prefixing option keys with '-' should be restored or the error message generation in `MissingOptionException` should be updated to add it back when constructing the message.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
